chapter: Six lost years and The White Album
title: Bandstand warriors
summary: He sees the bandstand as the place to settle disputes and names Tito Puente, Charlie, Tito Rodriguez and Machito.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I’m kind of speechless after all that. So maybe we’ll go back to the music. We’ll talk about the music. I mean, that’s...
Oh, we were talking about music?

Sure. This is just that what can happen in the career of a musician is not easy. You’ve got to have the will to take it and to dish it out, you know—and boy, did I take it! And then, when you dish it out, for me it was an outlet on the bandstand. I always had the most potent orchestras, the best of the musicians that I can find, and if something annoyed you about me, if you’re a musician, or between bands and that...between band lingo... Then we’ll let the bandstand decide. You know what I mean? Let’s go on the bandstand, and you’ll lay down what you’re going to lay down, and then I’ll come and I’ll do... Because I consider myself a bandstand warrior. One of the greatest bandstand warriors was Tito Puente. My brother, Charlie, Tito Rodríguez, Machito. And I don’t stay far behind.
I can only imagine that most of you all have to deal with this. Those were the days when stuff was really, really challenging.
Yup. And all the bands were happening.
